description: The European Ground Motion Service measures ground deformation across Europe from Sentinel-1 radar interferometry (InSAR), revealing subsidence, uplift, landslides and settlement. It is updated annually, with releases covering 2019 to 2023 and 2020 to 2024, and offers three product levels: Basic (level 2A), Calibrated (level 2B) and Ortho (level 3). It is run by the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service. Data are available through the EGMS Explorer, where searching and downloading require a login and only the latest two releases are kept; no licence is named on the pages read. Caveats: InSAR points depend on stable radar reflectors, so coverage is dense in built areas but sparse on vegetated ground, and motions are relative to reference points. It supports condition monitoring and subsidence or landslide hazard screening of railways, roads, dams, pipelines and buildings; a related record is AHN, the Dutch national elevation model.
